author: justanother90
quote: GTA VI – My First 12 Hours: A Beautiful ChoreAfter spending 12 hours with GTA VI, I’m left feeling incredibly disappointed. From an artistic and technological standpoint, the game is an absolute masterpiece. The visuals, environmental detail and technical achievements are phenomenal. Unfortunately, that doesn’t necessarily translate into an enjoyable gaming **** doesn’t feel like GTA as we once knew it. Many of the fundamental aspects that made the franchise so enjoyable appear to have been removed or watered down in favour of realism, mundane activities and restrictive storytelling.I spent much of my first eight hours running errands, buying groceries, getting flowers, making the house nice, painting walls, fixing a roof and diving for **** put effort into preparing for Lucia’s arrival, buy new clothes, get a haircut and go to pick her up, only to have her insult your appearance, criticise your car, practically ignore you at the bar and then act cold towards you back at the **** constant snide remarks, jealousy, emotional manipulation and unpredictability of Lucia blowing hot and cold make for a genuinely unpleasant experience.Having previously been in a manipulative and emotionally abusive relationship in real life, these interactions are disturbingly familiar. The behaviour is recognisable, and the fact that you’re seemingly locked into this relationship, without any meaningful ability to walk away or establish boundaries, makes it feel almost **** issue isn’t that Rockstar has chosen to portray a toxic relationship. It’s that the player appears to have no meaningful agency within it. There’s a considerable difference between exploring an abusive relationship through storytelling and forcing the player to actively participate in one without offering **** a franchise that was once synonymous with freedom, rebellion, chaos and escapism, this feels incredibly restrictive.I also can’t shake the feeling that certain aspects of the writing are trying to push an agenda rather than prioritising entertainment, compelling characters and natural **** contrast, I recently played through Ocarina of Time and had an absolute blast. It reminded me exactly why I love video games: adventure, discovery, freedom, escapism and, most importantly, fun.Somewhere in Rockstar’s relentless pursuit of realism, I feel they’ve lost sight of what made GTA so special. Realism should enhance gameplay, not come at the expense of enjoyment.I’m only 12 hours into the game, and I genuinely hope my opinion changes as the story progresses. But so far, I’ve spent more time admiring the technical achievements than actually enjoying **** VI feels like a technological masterpiece with an identity crisis. It’s beautiful to look at, but miserable to experience. Right now, it doesn’t feel like entertainment. It feels like a very expensive, exceptionally pretty chore.
